function: Learned (PPO) discrete allocation of IRS elements to Bob or eavesdroppers to maximise secrecy capacity under colluding and non-colluding eavesdroppers (p. 7)
system: Single LED transmitter, single-PD receivers (Bob plus two eavesdroppers), passive 15x15 mirror-array optical IRS on a wall, indoor VLC (400-790 THz band, DCO-OFDM) (pp. 1-3, 9)
method: PPO actor-critic reinforcement learning; policy and value networks with one 256-unit ReLU hidden layer; 1500 episodes, batch of 64 (pp. 7-8)
data_channel: Custom analytic indoor VLC model (modified Lambertian LoS plus specular IRS paths with delays), 5x5x3 m room, fixed user positions; no dataset (pp. 4, 8-9)
test_conditions: Training curves at 3 W; rates swept 1-10 W; each geometry (best, worst) and IRS size (15x15, 4x4) trained and evaluated on its own fixed positions (pp. 8-11)
baselines: Non-learned only: LoS-only link without IRS and All-Bob fixed allocation (all IRS elements to the legitimate user); no learned or optimisation baseline (pp. 9-11)
metrics: Achievable rates of Bob and eavesdroppers versus transmit power; secrecy capacity versus training episodes; percentage gains over baselines; analytic-versus-exact rate agreement (pp. 9-11)
complexity: Training complexity O(Nep·Nirs·(K+1)), O(1) per inference; exhaustive search (K+1)^Nirs; no runtime or parameter count (p. 8)
openness: none; no code or data link, only hyperparameters in Table 1 (pp. 8-9)
q1_support: p. 4: "modelled using the modified Lambertian expression"; custom analytic VLC channel (Lambertian LoS plus specular IRS paths), no standardized model (3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO) and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "records the best allocation vector abest observed during training, which is used in the numerical evaluation"; each geometry and IRS size is trained and evaluated on its own fixed positions (Figs. 4 and 7), with no unseen condition.
q3_support: p. 9: "the baseline where all IRS elements are allocated to Bob"; the baselines are non-learned only (All-Bob, LoS-only), and no earlier learned method (DQN, DDPG, other RL or neural network) is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "the training complexity scales linearly as O(Nep · Nirs · (K + 1))"; inference "O(1) complexity per inference".
q5_support: p. 8: "summarised in Table 1 to ensure reproducibility of the proposed approach"; only hyperparameters are given, with no code or data link, and the data come from the paper's own simulator (5 m x 5 m x 3 m room).
notes: Included as area 3: the learned function is the configuration of an optical mirror-array IRS (element allocation) for secrecy capacity; the goal is physical-layer security but the learned task is RIS configuration, so the function is borderline for the reviewer to confirm. Single-antenna VLC link, but the system exclusion does not apply because a RIS is present. The best allocation recorded during training is used for evaluation (p. 8), so the RL acts as a per-scenario search; only K=2 eavesdroppers are simulated. The channel follows ref. [16] (custom analytic model), not a standardized one.
